---
title: What the starter template is
description: The copy-and-own Rust service skeleton — what it contains, why it exists, and where it stands.
---

The starter template (milestone B1-T) is a small Rust service a product copies once and
then owns: a bounded HTTP layer, PostgreSQL with an owner/runtime role split and a
protections manifest, a copy-and-own accounts kit, the health contract, the host layer,
release and restore scripts, and the CI and evidence kit. It lives in the Backend
Platform repository under `template/` — its home because the repository's CI and evidence
kit already exercises it — and a copy depends on nothing here: no shared package,
service, login or database.

## Why it exists

The project's first milestone answered a question with evidence: do the sibling products
need a *platform*, or do they repeat the same slice of work? The memo's finding was the
slice — invite-gated sign-up, email verification, sessions, workspaces, members and
roles, API tokens, plan limits, deletion — while the independence rule (no product may
depend on a shared service) keeps a running platform from supplying it. The accepted
recommendation: stay parked, and ship the slice as code each product copies — the same
model they already use for UI code.

## What a copy contains

| Piece | What it is |
|---|---|
| `starter-http` | The bounded accept loop (connection cap *before* accept, header-read and idle timeouts, write-stall deadline, per-connection and lifetime caps, drain deadline) and the middleware stack (request ids, one error envelope, panics as 500s, request deadline, body limits, load shedding) |
| `starter-db` | The bounded pool, the owner/runtime role split, the startup gate (role → schema → protections manifest), binary/schema compatibility, fingerprints, the log-capture check |
| `starter-accounts` | The accounts kit: invite-gated sign-up, verification and reset through a mail port, sessions, sign-in budgets, workspaces, members and roles, API tokens, plan limits at admission, deletion |
| `starter-server` | Typed configuration (secrets from systemd credentials or owner-only files), the health routes, the wiring, the `starterctl` operator tool |
| `deploy/` | The hardened systemd unit (exposure 1.4), Caddy with TLS and bounds, journald retention, `env.example`, `harden.sh`, the development compose file |
| `scripts/` | The gate, the stack and dev loops, the restore drills, the upgrade rehearsal, `deploy.sh`/`rollback.sh`, `prove-limits.sh`, `load.sh`, pinned installers |
| `.github/` | The copy's own CI (SHA-pinned actions, daily) and Dependabot file |

It is an HTTP API with **no web interface** — a product's sign-in pages and dashboard are
its own, built on its copy of the workspace UI kit.

## Where it stands

Built and proven: the accounts kit, host layer (run on a CI VM with systemd), configuration
and secrets, releases and the schema gate, the health contract, the PostgreSQL, SQLite and
journal restore drills, the upgrade rehearsal (23 steps), the CI and evidence kit with 16
proven limits, the observability minimum, and upkeep.

Owed: the acceptance run — a product adopting a copy on a fresh droplet, timed against a
hand baseline; the Neon and bucket restore drills (no credentials yet); and a
quiet-machine load run (now dispatches to CI — see [the evidence kit](/template/evidence/)).

Next: [copy a template](/template/copying/), or read the [accounts API](/template/accounts/).
